content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a head structure to improve deep neural network for image classification.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
The proposed head structure can be easily integrated in multiple types of architectures for visual recognition providing improvement in recognition performance.


 Weaknesses:
1. The novelty is limited and there are some components of the proposed head that are not clearly motivated. For instance, there is no explanation of why the POCAs are aggregated via a summation and also why the summation is performing the best.

2. The number of parameters and the computational costs of the proposed head are directly depending on the number of classes. Although for a limited number of classes this can be acceptable, for tasks with very large number of classes (such as 50,000) this can become a serious bottleneck, thus limiting the applicability of the proposed approach.

3. The proposed head shows limited improvement in recognition performance for large networks and quite significant impact in increasing the relative parameters and computational costs on small networks.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper focuses on designing an effective head structure to improve accuracy of image classification. The paper presents a non-global attentive head called NOAH. NOAH contributes a novel form pairwise object category attention, consisting of feature map split, interaction, and aggregation operations. The paper applies NOAH to lightweight DNNs, MLP-tiny, and Deit-tiny, achieving improvement on large-scale datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:

(1)	The paper proposes a simple yet effective head for light deep frameworks to improve general image classification.
(2)	The paper validates the proposed NOAH on different deep neural networks, including Convs, MLP, and ViT on large-scale datasets.


Weakness:
(1)	The proposed head consists of feature map splits, pair-wise object category attention, aggregation operations. As far as I can see, the feature map split (split F into F_1, F_2,…,F_N ) is a group convolutional layer. As for the pair-wise object category attention, the only difference from conventional spatial attention is the split of F_{ki} and F_{vi} .
(2)	In page 5, the paper claims several differences with self-attention, but also has overlapping with existing techniques. For Points 1 and 4, spatial attention [r1,r2] is widely used. They also did not use query embedding. For point 3, it can be regarded as group Conv. I feel there is no novel points on the head. Although the paper achieves better performance against lots of baselines. I think the paper should implement existing various attention methods for comparison. Actually, I think the only difference could be is the split of F_{ki} and F_{vi} . 
(3)	In table 8, how about feature split on different backbones, e.g., MLPs and transformers?


[r1] Residual Attention Network for Image Classification, cvpr 2017.
[r2] Harmonious Attention Network for Person Re-Identification, cvpr 2018.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper proposes a new head structure for MLP, CONV, and transformers and validates the effectiveness of the proposed method. Overall, the experiments were performed with/without validation. The clarity is good. However, it also has overlapped techniques compared with the existing methods, for example, spatial attention methods. And the comparisons are not clarified. The technical contribution is not so strong.
content.summary_of_the_review:
(1) Missing analyses and discussions about some spatial attention.
(2) The proposed head could be regarded by group CONV and conventional spatial attention (feature split is different). I would like to see some responses about these concerns if I am not correct.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces a new head that can be easily plug-and-play in existing neural network architectures for image classification. The new head, named Non-glObal Attentive Head (NOAH), relies on pairwise attention to predict the object category. The experiments performed on ImageNet show that the proposed head improves performances for a lot of neural network architectures. The paper also contains a detailed ablation study of NOAH, which justifies a lot of design choices.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Strengths**

- This paper introduces a new head designed for the image classification task. This head is inspired from the dot-product attention. Unlike the popular dot-product attention, the proposed attention has only key and value inputs. The attention is computed only with the key input. Unlike the self-attention, the key and value inputs are not shared. The Hadamard product is used to combine the attention and values, while preserving the position information associated with the values. 
- The proposed head, NOAH, seems easy to plug-and-play into an existing neural network architecture. The experiment section shows the proposed head improves the performances on a lot of existing architectures: 10 CNN backbones, 8 ViT backbones and 8 MLP backones. The proposed head seems to be more effective for small neural network architectures. The analysis also shows that the proposed head can be used in a “from scratch training” regime and  in the fine-tuning regime.
- The paper contains a detailed ablation study of the proposed head to validate the contributions. The ablation study section shows an analysis of the key ratio (r) and the number of blocks (N). It also contains the results of different variants of NOAH which help to motivate some design choices. The paper analyzes the overhead of the proposed head. It shows a comparison of the number of parameters and multiply-add, but also the inference speed. 

**Weaknesses**

- I think the motivation and/or intuition behind the proposed head is not clear. The proposed head, NOAH, shows good results, but I am not sure to understand what is the problem solved to improve the performances. In other words, if NOAH is the solution, what is the problem that NOAH solves? I think answering this question will improve the quality of the paper.
- The attention is computed by using only the key inputs, but I am not sure to understand the meaning of the computed attention. It could be interesting to explain this design choice.
- The paper does not explain how the N non-overlapping feature groups are built. Are the groups randomly selected or are they built by using some locality constraints. It seems to be a part of the main technical contribution so the paper should clearly describe this part.  
- The proposed head seems limited to multiclass image classification, and it does not seem to be straightforward to adapt it to multilabel image classification. I think it will be great to add a comment about it in the paper, in particular if the proposed head is easy to adapt to the multilabel image classification task. 
- I think some claims in the paper are not well justified or overclaimed. For example in multiple parts of the paper, it is written “easy-to-optimize head” but there is no analysis that shows it. The current experiments show the proposed head is easy to integrate into an existing image classification network architecture, not that it is easy to optimize. I would suggest replacing “easy to optimize” by something like “easy to integrate in image classification network architecture”. Similarly, the abstract presents NOAH as “a simple and universal head structure, to improve the learning capacity of DNNs”, which is not well justified in the paper. The proposed head is evaluated only on multiclass classification benchmarks, not on multilabel classification benchmarks.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Overall, the paper is easy to read and understand, but I think the paragraph (“Formulation of pairwise object category attention.”) is a bit difficult to understand without reading (Dosovitskiy et al., 2021) paper. I would suggest rewriting some parts of this paragraph to be easier to read in a self-content manner. 

The proposed head, NOAH, seems novel but it seems to be limited to the multiclass image classification which limits the impact of the novelty. The performance of the proposed head is well studied with multiple multiclass image classification neural network architectures. 

The paper and the appendix have a lot of information about the implementation details. A lot of experiments are based on existing open source repositories so it should not be too difficult to reproduce the results.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper presents a head that seems novel and seems easy to integrate to existing multiclass image classification neural network architectures. The paper only focuses on the multiclass image classification task and ignores the multilabel image classification task, which limits the potential impact of the contributions. I think the paper does not present well the motivation and/or intuition behind the proposed head. Please check the Strength And Weaknesses section for more information.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This work introduced a global aggregation module for deep neural networks, namely Non-glObal Attentive Head (NOAH). Specifically, the final features are divided into some groups, where the features in each group separately perform spatial attention and feature mapping. Then, such these weighted feature maps with the same dimension of class number are aggreged by average along spatial dimension. The proposed method is adopted to deep CNNs, ViT and MLP-Mixer models, while experiments are conducted on ImageNet-1k dataset.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

+: The proposed NOAH brings performance improvement for various kinds of deep architectures on ImageNet-1k classification. 

+: The proposed method is easy to implement and brings a little of model complexity.

Weaknesses:

-: The motivation is not very clear.

(1) The authors claimed that ‘Because of the above factors, these methods are hardly ever used in the DNN architecture engineering, to the best of our knowledge’, which seems less rigorous. On the contrary, many global aggregation methods have been successfully adopted to deep architectures. Particularly, second-order pooling with fast normalization and feature dimension reduction can achieve clear performance gains for deep CNNs [iSQRT-COV, CVPR18], [R1] and ViTs [R2] on ImageNet classification and large-species classification.

[r1] Deep CNNs Meet Global Covariance Pooling: Better Representation and Generalization. IEEE TPAMI, 2021.

[r2] So-ViT: Mind Visual Tokens for Vision Transformer. CoRR abs/2104.10935 (2021).

(2) The proposed NOAH method performs spatial attention and feature mapping on each group feature, and the authors would better give more insight or theoretical analysis on effect or merits brought by such these operations. In other words, it seems not very clear why NOAH can achieve better performance, except extra spatial attention and feature mapping.

-: It seems not clear why features in each group are mapped into a feature space with dimension of class number (M)? How about effect of M? If M is number of classes, could the proposed method be flexibly adopted to large-species classification (e.g., iNat2017 [r3])?

[r3] The iNaturalist species classification and detection dataset. CVPR, 2018.

-: The experimental comparison could be further strengthened.

(1) Ablation studies are conducted using different models (e.g., ResNet-18 in Table 6&7 and ResNet-50 in Table 8&9). It would better to use the same model for evaluating effect of different factors.

(2) More SOTA and counterparts (e.g., higher-order pooling and attention models) could be compared.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The motivation of this work could be further clarified. The proposed NOAH involves off-the-shelf techniques (i.e., multi-head strategy, spatial attention and feature mapping via 1x1 convolution) brings performance improvement for various kinds of deep architectures on ImageNet-1k classification. The proposed method is easy to implement.
content.summary_of_the_review: This work introduced a simple global aggregation method to improve classification performance of DNN, which brings a little model complexity and performance gains for various kinds of deep architectures. However, motivation and theoretical insight of this work could be further clarified. Besides, experiments on feature dimension (M), large-species classification and SOTA comparison could be further strengthened.

content.title: NOAH: A New Head Structure To Improve Deep Neural Networks For Image Classification
content.TL;DR: This paper presents a simple and universal head structure to improve the representation learning of deep neural networks for image classification.
content.abstract: A modern deep neural network (DNN) for image classification typically consists of two parts: a backbone for feature extraction, and a head for feature encoding and class predication. We notice that the head structures of prevailing DNNs share a similar processing pipeline, exploiting global feature dependencies while disregarding local ones. Instead, this paper presents $N$on-gl$O$bal $A$ttentive $H$ead (NOAH), a simple and universal head structure, to improve the learning capacity of DNNs. NOAH relies on a novel form of attention dubbed pairwise object category attention, which models dense local-to-global feature dependencies via a concise association of feature split, interaction and aggregation operations. As a drop-in design, NOAH can replace existing heads of many DNNs, and meanwhile, maintains almost the same model size and similar model efficiency. We validate the efficacy of NOAH mainly on the large-scale ImageNet dataset with various DNN architectures that span convolutional neural networks, vision transformers and multi-layer perceptrons when training from scratch. Without bells and whistles, experiments show that: (a) NOAH can significantly boost the performance of lightweight DNNs, e.g., bringing $3.14%$|$5.30%$|$1.90%$ top-1 accuracy improvement for MobileNetV2 ($0.5\times$)|Deit-Tiny ($0.5\times$)|gMLP-Tiny ($0.5\times$); (b) NOAH can generalize well on relatively large DNNs, e.g., bringing $1.02%$|$0.78%$|$0.91%$ top-1 accuracy improvement for ResNet50|Deit-Small|MLP-Mixer-Small; (c) NOAH can still bring acceptable performance gains to large DNNs (having over 50 million parameters), e.g., $0.41%$|$0.37%$|$0.35%$ top-1 accuracy improvement for ResNet152|Deit-Base|MLP-Mixer-Base. Besides, NOAH also retains its effectiveness in the aggressive training regime (e.g., a ResNet50 model with NOAH reaches $79.32%$ top-1 accuracy, yielding $0.88%$ gain) and other image classification tasks. Code is provided for results reproduction.
